add.title: Inside jails, gay men and trans women ‘wed’ fellow PDLs to escape abuse (Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism, by Aie Balagtas See)
add.summary: Investigative feature on Manila City Jail: transgender women and gay men are held in the ordinary MALE dormitories (mandatory head-shaving on arrival for the male dorm), where they assume housekeeping/entertainer roles and informal same-sex “weddings” with male inmates are widely used by gangs as a survival/protection strategy against abuse. Documents that trans women in Philippine jails are housed by birth sex in male facilities with no gender-matched placement, and that safety comes from inmate hierarchies rather than policy.

add.title: BJMP-Davao transfers LGBT inmates to annex facility for safety (SunStar Davao, by Ian Carl Espinosa)
add.summary: Official practice documented: BJMP-Davao Community Relations chief Jail Senior Inspector Ellen Rose Saragena said LGBT detainees at Davao City Jail are relocated in batches to the City Jail Annex “to prevent abuse”, alongside persons with disabilities, the sick and senior citizens; three LGBT groupings live in the annex since its establishment. Shows the official Philippine response is administrative segregation of LGBT detainees into a separate annex for “safety”.
